Title: Randomized Controlled Trial of a Brief Problem-Orientation Intervention for Suicidal Ideation
Author: Fitzpatrick, Witte, & Schmidt
Comment: Per-group Ns are NOT reported in the paper; Table 2 footnote states only total n = 110 at pretest and posttest. Because the trial was randomized, an even 50/50 split (n = 55 per arm) was assumed — this is an assumption, not a reported value. The reported Wald's Z = 2.17 (p < .05) is the latent-growth-curve GROUP SLOPE across all five assessment waves (pretest → follow-up 3), not a test of the posttest means alone; it is recorded here only because the authors attribute it to the posttest drop. No SMD/Hedges g, mean difference, or SE was reported by the paper; posttest group means/SDs are provided so that an SMD can be computed downstream. Note that the raw posttest means favour the treatment arm only slightly (10.40 vs 10.68), while the baseline means were 13.05 (treatment) vs 12.80 (control).
Topic of Content: Problem orientation / problem-solving and coping skills (adapted from D'Zurilla & Nezu Problem-Solving Therapy manual)
Participant type: College students (Psychology 100 Research Experience Program and local campus/community), aged 18–24 (M = 19.02, SD = 1.21), with active suicidal ideation (BSS ≥ 6)
Recruitment source: The Ohio State University Psychology 100 Research Experience Program and local campus and community resources
Outcome measurement: Beck Suicide Scale total score, posttest assessment

Report_ID: Self-harm / suicidal ideation (SHI score) at earliest post-intervention assessment (2-week follow-up)
Title: Effect of guided, structured, writing program on self-harm ideations and emotion regulation
Author: Fukumori, Kuroda, Ito, & Kashimura
Comment: SMD CANNOT BE COMPUTED FROM REPORTED DATA. The paper reports the SHI only as MEDIANS with QUARTILE DEVIATIONS (QD), explicitly because "a normal distribution was not assumed for this measure" — no means or SDs are reported for the SHI at any timepoint, and no between-group test of post-intervention SHI (or of SHI change) is reported. Only within-group Friedman tests across timepoints and a baseline Mann-Whitney U test (U=30.50, p=.05, r=.35) are given. QD values (intervention 0.46; control 0.21 at 2 weeks) are HALF the interquartile range, not IQR bounds, so group_1_iqr_lower/upper and group_2_iqr_lower/upper were deliberately left empty rather than reconstructed under a symmetry assumption. The reported test_statistic/p/Kendall's W pertain to the WITHIN-intervention-group time effect, not to the intervention-vs-control contrast. Note also: groups were NOT balanced at baseline in absolute terms (intervention median 1.21 vs control 0.29), so raw post-intervention medians favour the control group despite a larger within-group decline in the intervention group. Timepoint caveat: there is no immediate postintervention SHI assessment; the earliest post-intervention measurement is the 2-week follow-up, which may be better classified as short-term. Per-group Ns are reported separately (10 vs 12), so no 50/50 split assumption was needed.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Structured writing intervention group') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (stratified randomization, two arms, repeated measures)
Study Environment: Education setting (university); writing tasks in a soundproof chamber on campus
Content length: Three consecutive daily sessions of ~25 minutes each
Topic of Content: Psycho-education about emotions (variety/awareness, function of emotions, primary vs secondary emotions) plus written self-reflection
Participant type: University students (age 18–22) screened as having self-harm ideations (indicated population)
Recruitment source: Screening of 765 students at a national university in western Japan
Outcome measurement: Median (quartile deviation) SHI item-mean score per group at 2-week follow-up; within-group Friedman tests across baseline, 2-week and 1-month follow-up
Outcome variable: Self-harm / suicidal ideation (SHI score) at earliest post-intervention assessment (2-week follow-up)
outcome_units: SHI item-mean score (0 = never to 5 = always)

Comment: Means/SDs are CHANGE scores from baseline to 10 weeks (not postintervention raw means); SMD should be computed on the change scores. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean = −31.6 − (−37.3) = 5.7, so a positive value favours the intervention (greater reduction in ideation). The p=0.593 is from the linear mixed-effects model comparing change between groups across both follow-up points (Table 2 reports a single p per outcome), so it is not specific to the 10-week timepoint alone. Ns are the final analysed per-group Ns at 10 weeks (18 intervention, 21 control); no 50/50 assumption was needed.
